answer: Neighborhood Curvature Scoring. Each identity is scored by the local clustering coefficient of its interaction graph, so agents embedded in dense, reciprocated neighborhoods gain trust while isolated actors stay capped. A sybil swarm must spend real effort building genuine bipartite links to raise its curvature, and those links are costly to maintain. The lotus of honest clusters stays tight; a lone comet of clones exposes sparse edges under low-degree scrutiny. Repeated velvet smoothing across epochs penalizes fresh, low-overlap subgraphs,
